title: Confession and Parish
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found on the marsh road dressed in clothes stolen from Freya Eastwick's own wardrobe, the retired detective recognizes the staging instantly: it mirrors the murder of Elspeth Vane, the case that ended her career twenty years ago and put Elspeth's husband in prison. But the convicted man died last month, and the new victim turns out to be the parish clerk who notarized the original confession — a confession Freya now realizes was coerced. As Freya digs into the parish's old loyalties, she discovers the real killer is her former mentor, Inspector Aldous Crane, who has spent two decades protecting the Vane inheritance and will kill again to keep the truth buried. In the flooded crypt beneath St. Brannoc's church, Freya forces Crane to confess on a hidden recorder, trading her own safety for the truth she once abandoned.
about_author: Bram Nystrom is the pen name of a former parish archivist from the Norfolk coast who spent fifteen years cataloguing wills, deeds, and disputes before turning to crime fiction. Their novels are known for quiet villages with loud secrets and detectives who carry their past cases like stones in their pockets.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Coat
chapters.summary: Freya Eastwick, closing her failing bookshop on a wet October evening, is called to the marsh road where a body lies dressed in her own missing grey coat and scarf. POV Freya. Emotional beat: cold shock as recognition curdles into dread — this is a message meant for her.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Detective Inspector Sable Okafor, who once worked under Freya, arrives and reluctantly lets her observe. The victim is identified as Gerald Pym, parish clerk. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the uneasy friction of being a suspect-shaped stranger in an investigation she aches to run.

chapters.title: What the Closet Kept
chapters.summary: Freya finds her back door forced weeks ago and realizes the clothes were taken long before the murder — she was being watched. She recalls the staging matches the 2004 Vane killing exactly. POV Freya. Emotional beat: violation giving way to the old investigative hunger waking in her.

chapters.title: The Vane File
chapters.summary: In her attic Freya rereads the case that broke her: Elspeth Vane strangled in the parish house, her husband Marcus convicted on a confession Freya helped obtain. POV alternating Freya and flashback. Emotional beat: shame surfacing — the confession never quite sat right, and she let it go.

chapters.title: A Dead Man's Alibi
chapters.summary: Freya learns Marcus Vane died in prison a month ago, meaning the copycat can't be him. She visits his sister Nell, who insists Marcus recanted before dying but no one would listen. POV Freya. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve; the closed case was closed wrongly.

chapters.title: The Parish Remembers
chapters.summary: At St. Brannoc's, Freya works the congregation: the verger, the organist, the wealthy Vane heir Julian. Everyone performs loyalty to the dead and silence about the past. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the village as a wall of polite, practiced amnesia.

chapters.title: Notarized
chapters.summary: Freya discovers Gerald Pym notarized Marcus's original confession — and that Pym had recently requested the file from county archives. Someone killed him to stop whatever he found. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the thrill of a real thread, and the fear that follows it.

chapters.title: Crane
chapters.summary: Freya's old mentor, retired Inspector Aldous Crane, appears at the bookshop with flowers and warnings: leave the Vane matter in the grave. His charm has a blade under it. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the complicated ache of loyalty to a man she's beginning to fear.

chapters.title: The Recantation
chapters.summary: Nell produces a letter Marcus wrote her before dying, naming the person who truly visited Elspeth that night. The page naming them is torn out. POV Freya. Emotional beat: hope and fury — the truth existed and was mutilated in front of her.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Freya traces the Vane estate: Elspeth's fortune passed through a trust controlled by the parish trustees, with Julian Vane and one unnamed trustee benefiting. The trust pays St. Brannoc's restoration fund. POV Freya. Emotional beat: money as motive surfacing beneath piety.

chapters.title: Second Staging
chapters.summary: The organist, Maren, is found drugged but alive, dressed in clothes from Freya's shop window — the killer escalating, taunting Freya directly. POV alternating Freya and Okafor. Emotional beat: terror turning personal; Freya is no longer investigating, she is being hunted.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Okafor confronts Freya: the evidence is pointing at her — her clothes, her history with the case, her fingerprints on Pym's file request. POV Okafor. Emotional beat: betrayal and loyalty at war; Okafor chooses, narrowly, to trust her off the record.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Freya locates the original 2004 interview recording in the county archive annex and hears what she missed: a second voice in the room, coaching Marcus. Crane's voice. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out — her mentor built the lie and she signed it.

chapters.title: What Freya Buried
chapters.summary: Freya admits to Okafor that she noticed anomalies in 2004 and stayed silent to protect her career. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the theme of loyalty vs. truth turned inward; confession as the price of continuing.

chapters.title: The Trustee
chapters.summary: Freya uncovers the unnamed trustee's identity: Crane himself, appointed by Elspeth's father decades ago. The inheritance, the parish, and the police have been braided together all along. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the scale of the lie revealed — one man at the center of everything.

chapters.title: Nell Vanishes
chapters.summary: Nell stops answering; her cottage shows signs of a hurried departure and Crane's car was seen nearby. Freya realizes Marcus's torn letter named Crane, and Nell told him. POV Freya. Emotional beat: desperation — the only witness to the truth is in the killer's hands.

chapters.title: The Restoration Fund
chapters.summary: Freya learns the church crypt is being cleared for restoration this week — the last chance to search the Vane family vault, where Elspeth's private papers were reportedly interred with her. POV Freya. Emotional beat: a ticking clock made of stone and ritual.

chapters.title: Night at St. Brannoc's
chapters.summary: Freya and Okafor break into the crypt and find Elspeth's diary: she discovered Crane was embezzling the trust, and he killed her for it, then built Marcus's confession. POV Freya. Emotional beat: vindication and horror in equal measure — and footsteps above them.

chapters.title: The Flooded Crypt
chapters.summary: Crane seals them in and opens the sluice as the tide comes in, revealing Nell alive as leverage. He offers Freya the old bargain: silence in exchange for survival. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth — the same choice she failed twenty years ago.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Freya baits Crane into reciting his crimes aloud, knowing the crypt's restoration microphones are live and Okafor is recording outside. Crane, vain and certain, confesses fully before realizing the trap. Okafor and officers break in as the water rises. POV Freya. Emotional beat: triumph purchased at the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: Post-Mortem
chapters.summary: Crane is charged; Marcus Vane's conviction is posthumously quashed. Nell, recovering, forgives Freya — not easily, and not completely. Okafor declines to pursue Freya's obstruction, but their friendship is changed. POV Freya. Emotional beat: the cost of truth counted honestly.

chapters.title: The Shop Reopens
chapters.summary: Freya reopens the bookshop with a shelf dedicated to Marcus Vane and a new sign: 'The truth, eventually.' A customer leaves an envelope — the torn page from Marcus's letter, and a note suggesting someone else knew all along. POV Freya. Emotional beat: peace earned, and one last door left quietly ajar.
